title: Serverless Architecture Patterns
description: Explore common serverless architecture patterns including CloudFront, S3, API Gateway, Lambda, and DynamoDB.

data.text: Serverless architecture lets you build and run applications without provisioning or managing servers. AWS provides the building blocks: compute with Lambda, APIs with API Gateway, storage with S3 and DynamoDB, and content delivery with CloudFront.

A very common serverless pattern is: CloudFront (CDN) delivers static assets from S3, while API Gateway routes API requests to Lambda functions that read and write to DynamoDB. This stack requires zero servers to manage and scales automatically.

data.caption: The classic AWS serverless architecture with CloudFront, S3, API Gateway, Lambda, and DynamoDB.

data.text: Serverless apps are naturally event-driven. When an image is uploaded to S3, it can trigger a Lambda function that creates a thumbnail. When a new user signs up, EventBridge can trigger a welcome email workflow. Events flow through services like S3, SNS, SQS, and EventBridge, with Lambda handling the processing.

A common serverless pattern is automatic image processing. Users upload images to an S3 bucket. An S3 event triggers a Lambda function that uses Sharp or Pillow to generate thumbnails. The original and thumbnail are stored in S3, and CloudFront delivers them to users worldwide.

data.title: Image Processing Flow
items: User uploads an image to S3 via a pre-signed URL
EventBridge or S3 triggers a Lambda function
Lambda generates a thumbnail and stores it in a /thumbnails folder
CloudFront serves both original and thumbnail with low latency

data.title: Serverless Advantages
data.text: No servers to provision, patch, or scale. You pay only for what you use. AWS handles availability, fault tolerance, and scaling automatically.

data.title: Build a Serverless Image Upload Flow
data.description: Set up an S3 bucket that triggers a Lambda function on image upload to generate a thumbnail.
steps: Create an S3 bucket for image uploads
Create a Lambda function with Python and Pillow installed
Configure S3 event notification to trigger the Lambda function
Write Lambda code to create a 200x200 thumbnail
Upload an image and verify the thumbnail is created
data.expectedOutcome: Uploading a JPG or PNG to S3 automatically creates a thumbnail in a separate S3 prefix.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: The classic serverless stack is CloudFront + S3 + API Gateway + Lambda + DynamoDB
Event-driven patterns use S3, SNS, EventBridge, and Lambda together
Image processing is a canonical serverless example
Serverless apps scale automatically and require no server management
data.takeaway: Serverless architecture is the default choice for new applications on AWS. It is simpler, more cost-effective, and scales better than traditional server-based approaches.
